title: Surgebox: compact admin utility suite + runbooks-to-stepflow transpiler
creator: Marco Liu
description: Goal: deliver a compact, permissioned admin utility (Surgebox) bundled with a transpiler that converts existing runbook documents into executable stepflows suitable for the operator UI and the runbook-runner service. Scope: (1) lightweight CLI + web surface for Surgebox commands (idempotent primitives for user/session safe actions), (2) runbook-to-stepflow transpiler that emits typed steps, input schemas, and guard checks, (3) integration points for RBAC + audit logging + KMS-signed step receipts, (4) telemetry hooks for cost/latency/error breakdowns and dry-run validation mode. Success criteria: Surgebox can run 12 canonical runbook scenarios (see checklist in Confluence) in dry-run mode with zero side effects; transpiler produces stepflows that 95% match hand-author semantics for common ops tasks (db failover, cache warm, model rollback); all Surgebox actions are logged to audit pipeline and surfaced in Console as traceable runlets. Non-goals: complete replacement of the legacy admin CLI in this cycle; complex orchestration (long-lived workflows) is deferred to follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: 1) CLI and web components installable via opsctl and accessible to RBAC group 'oncall-admin'. 2) Transpiler accepts markdown-style runbook files and outputs verifiable JSON stepflows with typed inputs. 3) Dry-run produces identical pre-check traces with no write ops in staging. 4) End-to-end PR merged, E2E smoke tests passing, and Grafana dashboard shows telemetry for at least 10 runs.
design_decisions: - Prefer small composable primitives over monolithic scripts to reduce blast radius and simplify permissioning. - Use transpiler approach (deterministic rules + heuristics) rather than full NL-to-code to maximize predictability and reviewability. - Emit stepflow with explicit guard clauses and idempotency tokens so replays are safe. - Use existing audit pipeline and KMS integration (no new secrets flow) to keep security surface minimal.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Tradeoff: stricter typing and guard clauses increase upfront work for runbook authors but reduce incidents caused by ambiguity. - Risk: incomplete transpiler heuristics could misinterpret informal runbook prose; mitigation: include a 'validation' CI step requiring human approval for changed transpiler outputs. - Risk: surface area overlap with legacy admin CLI; migration plan required to avoid user confusion.
implementation_notes: - Repo: platform/ops/surgebox. Initial branch surgebox/ENG-612987. - Key packages: surgebox-cli (Go), stepflow-transpiler (Python), web-shell (React/TypeScript). - Telemetry tags: surgebox.run_id, transpiler.rule_set, dry_run=true|false. - Use existing runbook fixtures from /infra/runbooks/canonical for unit tests. - PR #8421 contains the core transpiler logic and initial test harness.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for transpiler rules covering 30 canonical sentences. 2) Integration tests: dry-run against staging with mocked external effects. 3) Canaries: roll out Surgebox to a small oncall cohort with feature flag; gather feedback for 1 week. 4) Runbook regression tests executed nightly for changed runbooks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature-flagged internal beta for SRE and platform oncall. Phase 2: Expand to priority customers' support engineers. Phase 3: Default enable for org on ops-2026.04 release after 2 weeks of stability. Each phase gated by telemetry targets and postmortem-free window.
security_and_compliance: - All Surgebox actions will require a short-lived, JIT-signed admin token and be recorded in the existing auditlog (immutable). - Transpiler output is reviewed by a 'runbook approver' team before being executable in prod. - Security review required for CLI KMS usage and any new write-capable primitives.
open_questions: 1) Should Surgebox primitives be cluster-aware (auto-detect region/cluster) or require explicit targets? Proposal: default to explicit target to avoid accidental cross-cluster ops. 2) How do we version transpiler rule-sets and handle backward compatibility for previously emitted stepflows? Proposal: embed rule_set metadata and support fallback execution paths.
next_steps: 1) Merge transpiler prototype PR and add 10 more unit tests (assigned). 2) Wire audit + telemetry events and create Grafana panel. 3) Run internal beta test and collect runlet traces for validation. 4) Prepare runbook authoring guide and CI validation job.
